note: The ENFORCEMENT GAP registry. Vocabulary fixed by Justin 2026-08-08: a STANDARD is a rule we enforce; a SURFACE is a place enforcement can act; a MOMENT is when a surface acts; an ENFORCEMENT FINGERPRINT is a standard's recorded mapping of surfaces to moments plus what its violations look like; an ENFORCEMENT GAP is a recorded FAILURE-SHAPE — the way a violation slipped past a fingerprint. A gap is evidence about fingerprints, not about one standard: it is swept against EVERY fingerprinted standard so one failure upgrades every standard sharing the hole-shape. A sweep records the population it ran against, so adding a fingerprint STALES every sweep and forces the new standard to be checked against every known shape. See scripts/lint-enforcement-gap-records.mjs. Both terms are namespaced deliberately (external review pass 2, finding 6): bare `gap` already names *Architectural Agency in the Gap* in this constitution and bare `fingerprint` already denotes a routing identity in the system, so the unqualified words carry two meanings each.

gaps.shapeDescription: The moment is WATCHED — a live surface sits there and its stated population plausibly reaches the violation — and the violation passes anyway, and the surface records no per-decision verdict, so nobody can distinguish 'the rule fired and was overridden' from 'it never fired' from 'it fired and judged wrongly'. **The shape is the unauditability, not a claim about coverage.** (Corrected 2026-08-09: this field previously read "The moment IS covered" while the evidence field beneath it said coverage is unknown — the record asserting and withdrawing the same claim in adjacent fields, which review pass 5 caught and which is the internal contradiction this registry exists to make impossible.) A fingerprint has this shape when it names a surface that leaves no trace of what it decided.

evaded.standard: Self-Unblock Before Escalating (which carried NO enforcement fingerprint — see note)
evaded.how: **CORRECTED (review pass 4): this record originally said the failure evaded that article's FINGERPRINT. It had none — none existed anywhere at the time — so the record asserted a mechanism that did not exist, which is manufactured enforcement inside the registry built to catch it.** What actually happened, stated without the invented mechanism: five tone-gate rules classified `blocking` sit at the outbound moment — B15_CONTEXT_DEATH_STOP, B16_UNVERIFIED_WALL, B17_FALSE_BLOCKER, B18_AUTONOMY_STOP, B19_PARKED_ON_USER — the gate was demonstrably live (it held one of my own messages the same day), and the 2026-08-07 violation went through. **Whether any of those rules should have fired is UNKNOWN and unknowable from the record**, because nothing on disk captures which rules were evaluated or what each returned; the advisory log captures only the deterministic preflight layer (`advisories: []`, `action: "clean"`). The earlier phrasing said their populations "plausibly cover" the manifestation and then treated that as coverage. It is not: *Self-Unblock* withdrew the coverage assertion the same day on the evidence that its own motivating violation passed the live gate. **The shape this gap records is therefore the absence of a VERDICT RECORD, not a claim about what the rules cover.**

No standard carried a fingerprint until this window created the field, so nothing recorded before it can honestly have EVADED one. What these records actually document is a failure that got past whatever was in place, which is a weaker and true claim.

gaps.shapeDescription: A guard is constructed, enabled, and visible in every inventory while doing nothing — because its arm is unreachable, because another component releases the precondition it waits on, or because the thing it guards is absent. Existence checks and status surfaces report it identically to a working guard, and an injection test against it produces SILENCE, which reads exactly like a clean pass. correctionLog.what: GAP-alive-but-inert vs Iterative Audit to Convergence: matched -> unmatched
correctionLog.why: The MATCH was asserted from the shape of the citation without checking whether a negative control existed. It did. The sweep check accepted the verdict because a verdict requires a REASON and not EVIDENCE — a hole in this registry's own machinery, found by making the exact error the registry exists to catch, inside the registry, one hour after building it. Reasons are cheap; the pattern that produced the true finding four hours earlier was INJECTION-TESTING, and I skipped it here because the shape felt familiar. A precise diagnosis suppresses the second opinion, which is why it raises the bar for checking rather than lowering it.

gaps.shapeDescription: A dispatch withholds its ANSWER — satisfying the protocol on its face — while supplying, as established observation, the one PREMISE the answer turns on. The reviewer then tests everything except the load-bearing claim, because it arrived as context rather than as a question. The output looks like independent judgement and is not. A guard has this shape when it checks that a protocol is PRESENT rather than that the premises were withheld — presence of the ritual standing in for the property.

evaded.standard: A Dispatch Supplies the Question and Withholds the Answer
evaded.how: The sovereignty referral was convened precisely because its author benefits from the answer, and it carried the protocol correctly: the question was posed as an explicit a/b/c and the preferred answer was named as a hypothesis rather than a conclusion — which reads as bias-avoidance. But the dispatch also stated that the symptom "appears to be evaluated on every outbound message already ... a check on real behaviour rather than on the existence of anything." That is the single fact that would make (a) correct, it was supplied as observation, and it is FALSE — the judgement is gated behind a seventeen-phrase substring pre-filter. A reviewer who accepted the framing instead of reading the code returns (a) and makes exactly the manufactured citation the referral existed to prevent. **The referral caught it and said so, about its own convener.** scripts/lint-dispatch-withholds-answer.mjs cannot see it: it verifies the protocol's presence in templated dispatches, and this dispatch HAD the protocol.

gaps.residual: Nothing detects a planted premise. The lint checks protocol presence; only a reviewer reading the underlying code instead of the dispatch's framing catches it — which is what happened here, and is not a guarantee.

gaps.shapeDescription: A correction narrows the defect and then RESTATES the over-claim it was correcting, inside the sentence announcing the fix. The gap shrinks — often by a large factor — while the CLAIM stays at 100%, so the artifact that certifies the defect is gone is itself the new instance of it. It survives review because a reader checks whether the fix happened, not whether the fix's own description is now true. A guard or a record has this shape when its correction note asserts full coverage rather than the coverage actually attained.

evaded.standard: Verify the State, Not Its Symbol
evaded.how: Three instances in one day, in the same file, each while fixing the previous one, and NONE caught by me. (i) The deferral guard matched two numeric id forms in prose while its prose claimed to police tracked deferrals — 47% of the real population; caught by external review pass 1. (ii) The fix took the MARKER but kept the commit-time step's character class, which a SPACE terminates, so 25 live markers with a space, comma or parenthesis stayed invisible — 89% coverage, and the sentence announcing the correction said it saw the subject; caught by an independent lane that re-derived the count and refused to accept mine. (iii) The gap registry's own certification clause listed one limitation when four applied; caught by external review pass 2. The through-line is not carelessness about the mechanism — each mechanism genuinely improved — it is that the DESCRIPTION is written in the moment of relief at having fixed the thing, and nobody re-measures a sentence.
